clue.text: Counterpart of old Poe's 'Pit', revised edition

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the writer's name with its possessive S, taken as letters
an edition of a magazine is a number, as in 'the latest number'

explanation.surface: A reference to a new edition of Poe's tale 'The Pit and the Pendulum', perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Pit' look like a title, but it is plain letters for the anagram; 'edition' means an issue of a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Your equivalent in another team or organisation is the person holding the matching post, a synonym of counterpart.

clue.text: Group showing a bit of patriotism

indicators.note: only a small stretch of the next word is taken, with its letters left in order

explanation.surface: A band whose act displays a little national pride.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of three performers or things is a small group, so the word fits as an example.

clue.text: Mistake to indicate vocal disapproval of book

parts.note: an audience jeers by calling out boo

explanation.surface: A critic jeering a disappointing book.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for a blunder or silly error, so it is a synonym of mistake.

clue.text: Confiscate one million quid

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Seizing a fortune of a million pounds and a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize goods or property by legal authority, a straightforward synonym of confiscate.

clue.text: In hearing, one after another, chaps with time in detention

indicators.note: in hearing means we take how a phrase sounds when spoken rather than its spelling

parts.note: doing things one after another is doing them in turn
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Men in custody being heard one at a time, then serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held without trial, especially in wartime, is a form of detention or confinement.

clue.text: Domestic help in priest's residence, six-footer following Bible

indicators.note: following places the insect after the Bible abbreviation

parts.note: a manse is a minister's house, especially in Scotland
RV stands for the Revised Version of the Bible
an insect has six legs, and an ant is an example

explanation.surface: A household servant at the vicarage, a tall man, coming after the scripture reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but means an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A male servant in a household, such as a valet, is a kind of domestic help.

clue.text: Star could conceivably emerge from this ballet etc

parts.words: Star could conceivably emerge from this
parts.note: read the solution as wordplay: the letters of arts, when performing (worked over, rearranged), produce the clue's word star

explanation.surface: Stage schools and dance companies are where a star might be born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' acts as an anagram signal on ARTS, which gives STAR, so the solution is wordplay producing the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet, drama, music and opera are examples of the arts presented live to an audience.

clue.text: Teen hurt in port botched manoeuvre in road

indicators.note: a botched job is messed up, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A young person injured at a harbour after a bungled move on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning a car round in a narrow street using forward, reverse and forward moves is a driving manoeuvre.

clue.text: Fancy bankrupt to risk everything

parts.note: to fancy someone is to go for them
someone bankrupt is broke

explanation.surface: Someone attracted to a ruined gambler who stakes it all.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stake all you have on one attempt, risking everything.

clue.text: Fish ready with regular filleting

indicators.note: filleting removes parts at regular intervals, so every other letter of the word ready is kept

explanation.surface: A fish prepared for cooking by being filleted.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat cartilaginous sea fish such as the skate, so an example of a fish.

clue.text: Kind outsider in settlement?

definitions.meaning: a kind is a type or variety
a settlement of a problem is a ...-out, and in that phrase this word stands outside the word out

explanation.surface: A friendly stranger in a village community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective but is a noun; the second part plays on a sort-out, where this word sits on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Type, variety and category are all synonyms for kind used as a noun.

clue.text: Sound of skipper in foreign thoroughfare

indicators.note: sound of means we take how the word is pronounced, not its spelling

parts.note: a kangaroo skips along, and roo is its short form

explanation.surface: A ship's captain heard in a street abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipper' suggests a captain but means a jumping kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for street, so a thoroughfare in a foreign country.

clue.text: Washing that's best kept secret

parts.note: laundry suggests soiled sheets, but the idiom means private scandal you would not air in public

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for embarrassing private matters, from not washing soiled sheets in public.

clue.text: The insects stirred up irritability

indicators.note: things stirred up are mixed about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A disturbed swarm of insects grows irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being touchy and bad-tempered is a synonym for irritability.

clue.text: Extravagant expenditure — thing a soul has to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spendthrift needs to change their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb for spending freely, used here as a noun for lavish spending.

clue.text: Undesirable look about lively dance

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a leer is an unpleasant, suggestive look

explanation.surface: A lecherous stare at a spirited dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast Scottish or Irish folk dance, so an example of a lively dance.

clue.text: Traps repairer?

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth, so someone who fixes traps fixes mouths, not snares

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who treats teeth works on people's mouths, slangily called traps.

clue.text: Treason disturbed distinguished politician

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand statesman unsettled by an act of betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an upper legislative house, such as in Rome or the US, is a senior politician.

clue.text: Promotional material in back of lorry?

definitions.meaning: a short preview advertising a film
the towed rear section of an articulated lorry

explanation.surface: Advertising posters carried on the rear of a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a film preview and a towed vehicle behind a cab share this word.

clue.text: Promote in work, though not over hospital

indicators.note: though not tells us to take away the next item from the word before

parts.note: opus is Latin for a work, especially of music
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Advancing in your job, though not beyond the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To push a product or idea is to advertise and advance it, a synonym of promote.

clue.text: Irish and French director in circle proving troublesome

indicators.note: in places the director inside the circle

parts.note: a ring is a circle
Jacques Tati was a French film director

explanation.surface: An Irish and a French film-maker in the same group causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link: the French director is TATI, not ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annoying is troublesome, so the adjective fits the participle phrase.

clue.text: Take off cloak with cold gone

indicators.note: gone tells us the named letter disappears from the word

parts.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Removing a cape now the cold has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests removing clothing but means mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to imitate or mimic them, the verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Place to get round maybe in Minnesota

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the next word

explanation.surface: A spot to go round, perhaps in a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is a round of drinks, not a circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub where you might buy a round of drinks.

clue.text: No evidence of embargo in Scottish port

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing or none
an embargo is a ban

explanation.surface: No sign of any trade embargo at a harbour in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A west-coast Scottish town and ferry port, so an example of a Scottish port.

clue.text: Some young volunteers rejected in private fashionable set

indicators.note: in puts the young and volunteers inside the soldier

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
a litter is a group of young animals born together

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Young volunteers turned away from a private party of the smart set.
explanation.definitionFit: The celebrity crowd who are fashionable and glamorous form the glittering set.

clue.text: For instance, 27 also left

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: An example of a cross-reference, also left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer to 27 is a garden implement, so it is an example of an implement.

clue.text: Explorer removing top reveals emaciated figure

indicators.note: removing top takes away the first letter of a down answer

parts.note: Sir Francis Drake was an English explorer who sailed round the world

explanation.surface: An adventurer who loses his hat reveals a skeletal frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A very thin person is described as a rake, an idiom for an emaciated figure.

clue.text: Fast food maker is strain on company approved by Queen

parts.note: strain and pressure are synonyms
OK means approved
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A takeaway chef under stress from the firm, with royal approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast food' suggests takeaway meals but means food cooked quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealed pot that cooks food quickly under steam, a machine for speedy meals.
